subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Simulation Before Construction: Virtual Crash Tests
description: A quick win: understand Simulation Before Construction: Virtual Crash Tests.

hook.text: Car manufacturers crash-test thousands of virtual cars before bending a single piece of real metal.

buildup.text: Finite element analysis divides a structure into millions of small elements. Each element's response to force is then calculated.

discovery.text: A virtual crash test takes 8 to 12 hours of computing. A physical one takes weeks to prepare and costs $500,000 per test.

twist.text: Simulations are only as good as their models. The 2010 Deepwater Horizon cement model predicted success. Reality disagreed.

climax.text: Cloud computing now lets engineers run thousands of simulations overnight. Design iteration that took months now takes days.

punchline.text: Crash it virtually. Fix it digitally. Build it once. Build it right.

quiz.question: What is a key limitation of engineering simulations?
options: Computers can only simulate objects smaller than a car due to memory limits
Simulations are only as accurate as the models and assumptions they're built on
Virtual tests take longer than physical ones when accounting for setup time
